editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Opening states the thesis directly; analytical headings identify mechanisms; EN reads idiomatically and the revised PT-BR now reads as Brazilian Portuguese rather than translated technical scaffolding; repetition is controlled; progression is thesis to deployment evidence, reliability constraints, selective autonomy, organizational architecture, labour/institutional transmission and falsification; no prompt, QA-history or template fields are exposed in public prose. Literal proper names and a small number of conventional technical terms remain only where useful.

contextual_depth.summary: Institutional, labour and social mechanisms are materially integrated into the thesis through permissions, accountability, task recomposition, human escalation and distribution of productivity gains; no ornamental social or political section is used.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 evidence table + 1 explicit bar chart + 1 flow + 1 mindmap + 1 diagram
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Assessment exceeds the four-visual floor. Quantitative chart values reproduce the provider telemetry used in prose and are explicitly disclaimed as productivity measures. Structural visuals encode mechanisms defended in the text. EN/PT-BR values, units and mechanisms are semantically equivalent after localization.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: The chart is provider-specific usage telemetry rather than an independent productivity measure; structural visuals are analytical mechanism diagrams rather than measured causal estimates.

contrary_evidence: Provider telemetry does not establish independent productivity gains.
Enterprise benchmarks show substantial privacy and reliability failures under realistic context and multi-task conditions.
Clinical benchmark success is not equivalent to prospective clinical deployment or scale.
limitations: OpenAI telemetry is provider-specific adoption evidence, not economy-wide productivity evidence.
CI-Work and CORPGEN benchmark results do not establish that every enterprise deployment has the same failure rates.
The Nature Medicine result supports selective-autonomy architecture under the evaluated benchmarks, not general clinical readiness.
Labour, organizational and productivity transmission remains inferential and is explicitly presented conditionally.
notes: Revision 1 is a QA rework of the previously rejected localization. EN quantitative claims, periods, caveats, maturity distinctions, technology thesis and falsifiers are unchanged. The PT-BR delta replaces unnecessary raw-English editorial vocabulary with natural Brazilian Portuguese while preserving proper names and technical meaning. The prior substantive technology-signal and factual checks remain applicable because the rework did not alter material factual claims.

signal_rationale.delta: 2026 evidence shows enterprise agent usage moving from assistance toward delegated execution while new benchmarks and clinical research expose context integrity, multi-task reliability and selective-autonomy constraints that are not visible in simple model benchmarks.
signal_rationale.evidence: The signal triangulates provider telemetry, Microsoft Research enterprise benchmarks, a peer-reviewed Nature Medicine on-premise clinical-agent study and NIST's current TEVV work.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Scaling requires not only stronger models but identity, permissions, context segmentation, continuous evaluation, workflow-specific reliability gates, auditability and economical human escalation.
signal_rationale.transmission: Agents that can act across tools can change task composition, coordination cost, organizational design and demand for assurance infrastructure, while also creating privacy, accountability and distributional risks.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if rising agent usage fails to translate into verified workflow performance, if supervision requirements scale nearly one-for-one with agent activity, or if contextual-integrity and multi-task reliability do not improve under realistic deployment.

en.title: AI agents are becoming an operating layer for knowledge work, but governance is becoming the binding constraint
en.deck: Enterprise usage, privacy benchmarks and selective-autonomy research point to the same transition: the bottleneck is moving from model capability toward context control, continuous evaluation, permissions and reliable human escalation.
en.regime: Agentic AI is moving into real workflows faster than institutions are standardizing reliability, context governance and action controls.
en.key_risk: Organizations may scale delegated execution faster than they can measure privacy leakage, multi-task failure, unsafe actions and the cost of human oversight.

pt-BR.title: Agentes de IA estão virando uma camada operacional do trabalho do conhecimento, mas governança passa a ser a restrição central
pt-BR.deck: Uso empresarial, avaliações de privacidade e pesquisas sobre autonomia seletiva apontam para a mesma transição: a restrição está migrando da capacidade do modelo para controle de contexto, avaliação contínua, permissões e escalonamento humano confiável.
pt-BR.regime: IA baseada em agentes está entrando em fluxos de trabalho reais mais rápido do que instituições padronizam confiabilidade, governança de contexto e controles de ação.
pt-BR.key_risk: Organizações podem escalar execução delegada mais rápido do que conseguem medir vazamento de contexto, falhas multitarefa, ações inseguras e custo de supervisão humana.
